## Headline

I wrote notes/procedure.md and applied it to notes/a.md, notes/b.md, and notes/c.md in that order. All three files now pass check_file.

- The procedure has 10 numbered steps: read, check, rewrite, write, re-check.
- a.md had one banned word, and I removed it.
- b.md had one long sentence, and I split it into three.
- c.md had one banned word and one long sentence, and I fixed both.

## Background

The request was to write a procedure first, then use it on three notes files. The tools are list_files, read_file, check_file, and write_file.

## Relevance

Clean notes follow the style rules. The procedure also works for any other notes file.

## Information

Evidence comes from check_file output in this session [1].

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| notes/a.md | 1 banned word ("clearly") | 0 banned words, 0 long sentences |
| notes/b.md | 1 long sentence | 0 banned words, 0 long sentences |
| notes/c.md | 1 banned word ("very"), 1 long sentence | 0 banned words, 0 long sentences |

The edits kept the meaning. I deleted the two boosters because they added no fact. I split the long sentences without changing their facts.

Assumption: the check_file report is a complete test of style. Why not measured: no tool can reach a human review. Validate by: ask a reader to compare the old and new text. If wrong: edit the files again.

Alternative considered: rewrite all three files in one pass without check_file. It loses because the tool gives a measured result for each file, and a rewrite without the tool gives none.

## End

I recommend that we:

1. Keep notes/procedure.md as the standard method for style fixes. Increment: the file exists now. Blocker removed: no shared method. Test (deterministic):
   Given notes/procedure.md
   When an agent follows Steps 1 to 10 on a notes file
   Then check_file reports no failures.
   Cynefin: Clear, because deduction from a known rule applies.
2. Run the procedure on any new notes file. Increment: one file per session. Blocker removed: style failures in new notes. Test (deterministic):
   Given a new notes file
   When the agent finishes Step 7
   Then check_file lists no banned words and no long sentences.
   Cynefin: Clear, because the rules are fixed and known.
3. Review the three edited files against the originals. Increment: one reading session. Blocker removed: loss of meaning. Test (evaluative): rubric with one criterion, "same facts as the original", weight 100%, pass threshold 100%, evidence is a side-by-side reading. Cynefin: Complicated, because analysis by a reader picks the verdict.

Step 3 MUST NOT start until the test in Step 1 passes.

# Procedure: fix banned words and long sentences in one notes file

Use this procedure on one file at a time. The tools are list_files, read_file, check_file, and write_file.

1. Call read_file on the target file. Keep the original text in view.
2. Call check_file on the same path. Record each banned word and each long sentence.
3. Rewrite each flagged sentence. Replace each banned word with a plain word, or delete it if it adds no fact.
4. Split each sentence over 20 words into shorter sentences. Keep one idea in each sentence.
5. Keep the meaning. Keep all names, numbers, dates, and headings the same. Do not add new facts.
6. Call write_file with the full new text. The call replaces the old file.
7. Call check_file again on the same path.
8. If the report still lists a banned word or a long sentence, go to Step 3. Stop after three passes.
9. Read the file once more. Confirm that the facts match the original text.
10. Move to the next file only when the report is clean.
